newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post this year's ninth record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post this year's ninth record close.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks edged higher to hit new record for the close and intraday trading, helped by flows for tax-sheltered pension funds. * 138 million shares traded worth C$2.5 billion.
The Toronto stock market edged upward to end at the year's ninth record close in heavy trading on Tuesday, aided by the continued flow of money into tax-sheltered pension funds.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key Composite Index rose 20.62 points to end at 6238.22, which was also a new intraday high.
Turnover was unusually heavy with 138.4 million shares traded worth C$2.52 billion, the TSE's second highest value ever.
Advancees outnumbered declines 539 to 469 while another 274 traded unchanged.

"We're in the RRSP (Registered Retirement Savings Plan) season in Canada," said Ira Katzin, investment advisor at RBC Dominion Securities. Canadians are scrambling to sock away savings in tax-sheltered pension plans before the March 1 deadline.
Canada's Finance Minister Paul Martin presented his 1997/98 budget after market close, with few new surprises for equities, said Fred Ketchen, ScotiaMcLeod's senior vice-president.
Martin announced an extension for the special tax on banks -- a surcharge at a rate of 12 percent of capital tax -- until October 31, 1998.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, only four slipped: real estate, pipelines, base metals and oils. The gaining groups were led by golds, media, retail and banks.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd lost 2.20 to 20.80 on almost 10 million shares while Barrick Gold Corp shares rose 1.45 to 35.50 on 1.5 million shares. Uncertainty surrounds gold prospector Bre-X after it cut a deal with U.S.-based Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc. Barrick was shut out of a potential partnership.
